newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: HOLYMAN SHARES DIVE AFTER DOWNGRADE.
newsitem.headline: HOLYMAN SHARES DIVE AFTER DOWNGRADE.

text.p: Shares in shipping group Holyman Ltd fell in light volume to A$2.70, a 17 month low, following a downgrade in profit forecasts for calendar 1997.
Holyman said it had reduced its year net profit forecast to the range of A$11.5 million to A$13.5 million from a A$14 million to A$16 million range predicted on June 6.

The company cited below expectations from its 67 percent owned U.K. division Holyman Sally as the reason for the downgrade, adding that half year profit to June 30 would be materially affected by Holyman Sally's results in that period.
The remainder of Holyman Sally is owned by Silja Oy Ab of Finland.
However, Holyman noted that excluding Holyman Sally, other units were performing in line with existing forecasts.

By 12.10 p.m. (0210 GMT) in a sharply lower overall market, Holyman shares remained 42 cents lower at A$2.70 on light turnover of 60,272 shares. But their bid/ask had dipped below this level to A$2.55/2.65.
